article.title: Xi, Putin, and Trump meeting concludes with vague commitments, but strong symbolism
article.author: Abdul Rahman
article.content: Chinese President Xi Jinping held the first ever trilateral summit of Russia, China, and the US on the sidelines of the ongoing Asia-Pacific Economic Council (APEC) summit in Shenzhen on Thursday, November 19. The meeting, attended by Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump, ended with a joint Declaration towards Peace with all three countries agreeing to find ways to work together on common issues including the need for reforms in the UN, global energy security, and rising nuclear risk. The declaration also talked about the principles of the operation of the International Criminal Court (ICC) and underlined the immunity for top state officials. The declaration emphasized that the reforms in the UN are necessary for it to make effective interventions to issues of global concern and to fulfill its mandate of preserving global peace and security. The point was an indirect reflection on recent failures of the UN to make any meaningful intervention in the global conflicts particularly its failure to prevent the Israel’s genocide in Gaza, the war in Ukraine and the US-Israeli war on Iran. All three countries also agreed that they should work together to reduce the risks of a nuclear war breaking out. They underlined the need to conduct dialogue for reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons. The three heads of states also agreed it was necessary to maintain the global flow of energy and to minimize the disruptions to global energy supply chains even during conflict and to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum to ease constraints on general production and prices. Thycydides trap is not destiny During his speech in the summit, hinting towards recent conflicts, Xi pointed out that there must be peace among major countries in the world in order to maintain global stability and to avoid chaos. Asking for a more friendly and trust based relations between the great power Xi denounced the conventional notions of great power rivalry repeating that the so-called “Thucydides Trap is by no means a destiny.” Thycydides, an ancient Greek historian, is often quoted to describe conflicts and rivalries between a rising power and an established one. As major countries and the permanent members of the UN Security Council China, Russia and the US must work together to meet global challenges and jointly uphold world peace and stability. They together can make greater contributions to the progress of humanity, Xi argued. Xi recalled how China, Russia and the US have worked together in the past to save the world from fascism during the Second World War claiming the same coordination is required now to “steadfastly safeguard the postwar international order, uphold the purposes and principles of the UN charter, and defend the hard-won outcomes.” Xi proposed a four point code of conduct for the great powers to work together; mutual respect, peaceful coexistence, win-win cooperation and dialogue and consultation. For working together it is necessary that all the countries respect each other’s social structure and distinctive development paths adopted without trying to impose each other’s preferences over the other, Xi underlined. He also emphasized the UN principles of respecting each others’ sovereignty, territorial integrity and non-interference in domestic affairs as fundamental for good relations. “On major sensitive issues concerning one another, it is important to communicate in advance, try to see things from one another’s perspective, act with caution, and in particular, not to challenge the red lines of one another,” Xinhua reported Xi saying. Pointing towards the rising risks of nuclear conflicts and its possible impact on the existence of humanity, Xi talked about the need to push for complete nuclear disarmament. “Nuclear weapons, the Sword of Domcleas that hangs over humanity, should be completely prohibited and thoroughly destroyed over time to make the world free of nuclear weapons,” the Chinese leader said. Greater communication and coordination Indirectly referring to the impacts of US policies on global trade, Xi said that “decoupling and disruption of industrial and supply chains are not the ways to go” calling for stronger communication and coordination to “safeguard the security and stability of the global” markets. Both the US-Israeli war on Iran and Ukraine war have disrupted global supply chains of energy products. While Iran has restricted movements through the Strait of Hormuz in response to the US-Israeli war, Russia has been prevented from exporting freely due to sanctions and attacks on energy installations. Trump and Putin agreed with Xi’s call for a joint effort to push the countries to resolve their disputes through diplomatic channels with Putin emphasizing on “shared responsibilities” and calling for “proper resolution” of all “hotspot issues.” Trump claimed the three countries, the biggest military powers with the largest number of nuclear arsenals in the world, were “making history” by correcting a historical mistake of great powers not talking to each other.
